hippo-msk-Q32.answer:
Shoulder adduction, extension and internal rotation, with elbow flexion.

Break the position down joint by joint. The elbows are bent, so elbow flexion. The humerus swings behind the trunk, which is shoulder extension. The forearms turn inward so the hands meet at the small of the back, which is internal (medial) rotation. Bringing the two wrists together behind the body draws the arms toward the midline, which is adduction, not the abduction the source printed. The muscle notes put this exact combination in one muscle: latissimus dorsi (from 02.1 - Anatomy of the Back & Neck) "extends, aDDucts and medially rotates the humerus". That is the hand-behind-the-back movement, and why the lats and teres major are what the cuffs load.

module-msk-Q154.answer: Sjögren's syndrome. Severe dry eyes (keratoconjunctivitis sicca, here bad enough to ulcerate the cornea) and a dry mouth (xerostomia, causing repeated dental caries) are the sicca features of Sjögren's, an autoimmune attack on the lacrimal and salivary glands. An inflammatory polyarthritis of the wrists and MCPs is a common extraglandular feature. Rheumatoid arthritis explains the joints but not severe sicca, although Sjögren's can be secondary to RA, SLE or systemic sclerosis.

module-neuro-Q60.answer: Acute onset (45 minutes ago) of an expressive aphasia with right face and arm more than leg weakness. The timing says vascular: a deficit that is maximal at onset is a stroke until proven otherwise. No verbal output while still following commands is an expressive (Broca's) aphasia, not a receptive or global one. Face and arm worse than leg, with full fields and no neglect, places it in the left hemisphere, in the territory of the superior division of the left MCA.
